name: Aloe vera
short: Oral aloe is linked to diarrhoea, low potassium and kidney failure; a case report describes hepatitis. Whole leaf extract is classed as a possible human carcinogen (rat data).
text: A toxicity review reported that swallowing aloe preparations is associated with diarrhoea, low blood potassium (hypokalemia), pseudomelanosis coli, kidney failure, phototoxicity and hypersensitivity reactions. The same review noted that aloe vera whole leaf extract showed clear evidence of carcinogenic activity in rats and is classified as a possible human carcinogen (Group 2B). A case report describes acute hepatitis in a 73-year-old woman, assessed as possibly to probably caused by oral aloe vera, with liver markers returning to normal after it was stopped; a review of supplements and bleeding found aloe vera loosely associated with surgical bleeding independent of anticoagulants. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
